findings.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — [P2, confidence 75] `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` omits the runtime `SiteSetting.default_locale` that now determines fallback resolution, so changing the site locale leaves previously cached missing-key translations serving the old locale until the process reloads.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:20 — [P1, confidence 100] `def ensure_loaded!; self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }; end` is invoked only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and other non-controller server paths load only the requested locale through `translate_accelerator` and return a missing translation when the key exists exclusively in the configured site-locale or English fallback.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — P1, confidence 75: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs only in the controller callback, so a background job or mailer translating before an HTTP request has loaded the site-default and English YAML files returns a missing-translation result instead of the configured fallback.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — P2, confidence 75: `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` omits the site-default fallback locale, so changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` leaves previously cached missing-key translations serving text from the old fallback until the cache is explicitly cleared.

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — [P2, confidence 75] `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` omits the runtime `SiteSetting.default_locale` that now determines fallback resolution, so changing the site locale leaves previously cached missing-key translations serving the old locale until the process reloads.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a caching issue. Looking at the diff, the new FallbackLocaleList class uses SiteSetting.default_locale as part of the fallback chain (line 17: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`). However, in translate_accelerator.rb, the cache key at line 72 (not shown in diff but referenced) uses `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` which doesn't include SiteSetting.default_locale. Since the fallback resolution now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (which can change at runtime), cached missing-key translations could return stale results from the old fallback locale. This is a real caching bug introduced by the new fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:20 — [P1, confidence 100] `def ensure_loaded!; self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }; end` is invoked only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and other non-controller server paths load only the requested locale through `translate_accelerator` and return a missing translation when the key exists exclusively in the configured site-locale or English fallback.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale` (line 158 in the diff). The `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` method loads all fallback locales (user locale, site locale, English). However, background jobs, mailers, and rake tasks don't go through ApplicationController, so they won't call `ensure_loaded!`. Looking at `translate_accelerator.rb`, the `translate` method only loads `config.locale` (line 64), not the fallback locales. This means non-controller paths would fail to find translations that exist only in fallback locales (site default or English) because those locales aren't loaded. This is a real bug in the fallback mechanism.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `ensure_loaded!` is only called in `set_locale` which is a controller callback. Looking at the diff, the `FallbackLocaleList` class defines `ensure_loaded!` method that loads locale files for fallback locales. However, this method is only invoked from `application_controller.rb:159` in the `set_locale` method. Background jobs and mailers that use I18n translations would not go through this controller callback, meaning fallback locales (site default and English) may not be loaded when translations are attempted outside of HTTP request context. adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real caching issue. Looking at the diff, the new FallbackLocaleList class in config/initializers/i18n.rb returns fallback chains that include SiteSetting.default_locale. However, in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb, the cache key at line 72 (visible in context) uses `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` which doesn't include the site default locale.
